Reviewed callback acceptance is separate from these results.

C and C++ generators check `Fin` arguments of a returned Lean closure before invoking it, including bounds inside structural containers, plain records and variants. They also preserve bounded values that Lean produces as closure results or host-callback arguments. A returned closure rejects an argument at or above its bound with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`; C++ throws `Error`. The Lean adapter independently constructs each `Fin` from a decidable proof and returns `none` on rejection. It never substitutes a default. `Fin 0` rejects every value. A host callback returning a refined value remains unsupported, as do nested callbacks and a refined ordinary argument beside a callback. Other native targets require their own adapters. Fresh Lean adapter checks cover these directions; the C/C++ installed package gate remains pending.
